name: Jaipur
context: Bright block prints and bandhani feel at home here; heritage hotels dress up in the evening. Days are hot and dry, evenings cool down fast in winter.
tips: Cover shoulders and knees for forts, temples and havelis.
Desert evenings drop 10°C+ from the afternoon — carry a light layer even in summer.
Dust and sun: cottons and light dupattas over heavy silks by day.

name: Goa
context: Beach casual — linen, light cottons, breezy silhouettes. Shacks by day, dressed-up dinners by the water at night.
tips: Humidity is constant: skip polyester and heavy silks entirely.
One dressy evening look goes a long way; everything else can be relaxed.
Churches and temples still expect shoulders covered — a scarf or shirt does it.

name: Bengaluru
context: Mild all year, cool mornings and evenings. Offices run smart-casual; ethnic-fusion is common on Fridays and at team dinners.
tips: Carry a light jacket or shrug — AC and evenings both bite.
Sudden showers from June to October: quick-dry fabrics, avoid crisp cottons that crease.
Breweries and rooftop dinners are relaxed; one polished look covers the closing dinner.

name: Mumbai
context: Humid and fast-moving; clean lines and breathable fabrics. Monsoon (June–September) means real rain, not drizzle.
tips: Linen and cotton only in monsoon; carry a change if you have an evening plan.
Locals and cabs are hot — sleeveless under a light layer works best.
Evening in Bandra or Colaba: one sharp look, minimal jewellery.

name: Delhi
context: Extreme seasons — 45°C in May, 5°C in January. Weddings and dinners lean dressy; more embroidery and colour than the west coast.
tips: Winter trips need real layers: shawls, jackets, a warm dupatta for outdoor events.
Summer: loose cottons, cover up against sun and dust.
Delhi dresses up — err on the fancier side for evening plans.

name: Kochi
context: Warm, wet and green. Backwaters and beaches by day; temples and churches ask for modest dress. Kasavu (cream and gold) is the local aesthetic.
tips: Cream and white cottons look right here and stay cool.
Temples: sarees or long kurtas with dupattas; some restrict entry otherwise.
Pack for rain any month — a light cotton dupatta doubles as cover.

name: Manali
context: Cold year-round by Indian standards; nights near freezing outside summer. Layering matters more than any single piece.
tips: Base + warm layer + jacket. Woollen shawls and kurtas with jackets work well.
Skip sheer fabrics and chiffon — wind cuts through them.
One warm ethnic layer covers temple visits and dinners.

name: Leh
context: Dry, cold, intense sun. Only worth planning from May to September; layers on and off through the day.
tips: Wool and thick cotton over everything else; carry a windproof layer.
Monasteries: shoulders and knees covered.
Sun is fierce at altitude — full sleeves and a scarf.

name: Darjeeling
context: Cool, misty, often drizzly. Layers and closed shoes; nothing needs to be formal.
tips: A warm shawl or jacket every day; mornings are the coldest.
Monastery visits: modest, shoulders covered.
Quick-dry layers beat heavy wool when it drizzles.

name: Ooty
context: Cool and damp, much colder than the plains below. Casual throughout; a warm layer for evenings.
tips: Light woollens or a jacket over cottons; nights dip to single digits in winter.
Mist and drizzle most months — nothing that stains or clings when wet.
Estate walks: full-length bottoms and closed shoes.

name: Varanasi
context: Temple town — modest dress everywhere, sarees and long kurtas fit right in. Ghats at dawn are cool; afternoons hot.
tips: Cover shoulders and knees at all times in the old city.
Cotton and handloom; Banarasi silk only for an evening you plan for.
A large dupatta does temple, ghat and sun duty.

name: Agra
context: Monuments mean hours in the sun; comfortable, covered cottons photograph well against marble and sandstone.
tips: Solid colours photograph best at the Taj — avoid busy prints for that morning.
Cover shoulders for mosques within the monument complexes.
Winter mornings are foggy and cold; carry a shawl.

name: Rishikesh
context: Ashram and river culture — modest, easy cottons; evenings by the Ganga are cool.
tips: Ashrams and ghats: shoulders and knees covered, no sheer fabrics.
Cotton kurtas with pyjamas or palazzos do everything here.
Rafting or trekking days need separate activewear — pack outside the wardrobe plan.

name: Amritsar
context: Golden Temple requires head cover and modest dress; bold phulkari colour is the local language.
tips: Head cover for the Golden Temple — a dupatta or stole per day.
Winter fog and cold: heavy shawls and full sleeves from November to February.
Food-heavy trip: relaxed waistlines are a kindness.

name: Hyderabad
context: Dry heat; old-city elegance in pearls and chikankari. Corporate parks in the west run business casual.
tips: Charminar and Chowmahalla: modest cottons, comfortable footwear.
Evenings are dressier than Bengaluru — one embellished layer earns its place.
Summer afternoons hit 40°C: sleeves for sun, not warmth.

name: Kolkata
context: Handloom and cotton sarees, red-and-white palettes during Durga Puja, humid most of the year.
tips: Tant and khadi over anything synthetic — humidity is relentless.
Durga Puja trips: red, white and cream; pandal-hopping means walking shoes.
Winter (Dec–Jan) is pleasant: light shawls in the evening.

name: Chennai
context: Hot and humid with strict temple etiquette; Kanjeevaram and cotton sarees are the local register.
tips: Temples often require sarees, half-sarees or long kurtas with dupattas; shorts and sleeveless are refused.
Cotton only by day; silk for a temple or family evening.
Pondicherry's French Quarter is relaxed — linen and light dresses work.

name: Andaman
context: Beach and boat days; humid and bright. Nothing formal, one dinner look at most.
tips: Quick-dry cottons and linen; salt and sun ruin silk.
Cover-ups over swimwear for ferries and markets.
Evenings are relaxed — a breezy kurta or dress is the dressiest you'll need.

name: Ahmedabad
context: Dry heat, craft-heavy aesthetic — bandhani, ajrakh, mirror work. Navratri season is a nine-night wardrobe event.
tips: Kutch days are hot and nights cold in winter — pack a proper shawl.
Navratri trips: lehenga-cholis or chaniya with dupatta for garba nights.
Dry climate is kind to silks; heavy fabrics are fine in the evening.

name: Lucknow
context: Chikankari's home — light, elegant, understated. Hot summers, cold foggy winters.
tips: White and pastel chikankari kurtas fit both heritage walks and dinners.
Winter needs full layers; fog lingers till noon.
Imambaras: modest dress, heads covered inside.
